name: Call QA — Soft Skills / Technical Skills (4-item build + coaching + manager review + score bands + honest-ownership fix)

score_bands.applies_to: Any 0-100 weighted score -- per-call score or the aggregate Agent Pulse score shown on the dashboard.

bands.label: Star Performer
bands.manager_guidance: Call out publicly, use as a coaching example for the team.

bands.label: Excelling
bands.manager_guidance: Strong and consistent -- reinforce what's working, don't just move on.

bands.label: Solid Performer
bands.manager_guidance: On track. Normal coaching cadence, nothing urgent.

bands.label: Developing
bands.manager_guidance: Room to grow, not urgent. Pair with the specific coaching_note from the lowest-scoring dimension.

bands.label: Needs Improvement
bands.manager_guidance: Worth a 1:1 this cycle. Not yet a crisis, but don't let it sit.

bands.label: Needs Immediate Attention
bands.manager_guidance: Manager review is auto-triggered at this band.

score_bands.note: Bands are display labels only -- the underlying weighted score is what's stored and trended. Bottom boundary (60) is deliberately the same number as manager_review_policy.triggers.low_overall_score.threshold.

coaching_delivery_and_pattern_policy.delivery_routing: verdict='pass' -> agent_dashboard directly (reinforcement). verdict='partial'/'fail' -> manager_queue first -- manager decides how/when to raise it with the agent, consistent with this project's existing '1:1s should open a conversation, not put someone on the defensive' principle.
coaching_delivery_and_pattern_policy.confidence_spot_check: LLM responses should include a 'confidence' field (high/medium/low). confidence='low' or missing routes to a human spot-check queue rather than being trusted outright -- cheap addition, meaningfully improves trust without changing how verdicts are scored.
coaching_delivery_and_pattern_policy.weekly_digest: Per-call notes are NOT the agent-facing delivery format -- roll up weekly per agent, grouped by dimension. 2+ non-pass instances on the same dimension in a week fold into one pattern statement instead of repeating near-identical notes. Needs real call history to be meaningful -- implemented and ready, not demoed live with sample data for that reason.
coaching_delivery_and_pattern_policy.repeat_pattern_in_prompt: When a dimension has been flagged 3+ times for an agent within the recent window, that context gets INJECTED into the LLM prompt generating the current call's coaching_note, so the note itself references the pattern rather than the dashboard being the only place that knows about it. Threshold (3) needs calibration.

manager_review_policy.description: Two independent triggers route a call to manager review. Either can fire alone -- a call can also trigger both at once.
manager_review_policy.routing_note: Separate queue from coaching_note delivery -- never fold manager review payloads into the same agent-facing dashboard feed as routine coaching notes.

coaching_output.prompt_addition: Return a `coaching_note` field: 1-2 sentences, specific to this call, addressed to the agent. On 'pass', reinforce the specific behavior that made it correct. On 'partial'/'fail', name the specific moment that should have gone differently. Never generic.

dimensions.name: Ownership & Next Steps
dimensions.design_rationale: A rep often has zero control over WHO fixes an issue -- that's resolution_effectiveness's job, already escalation-aware. This dimension only tests whether the handoff was made concrete. The step-2 branch below exists specifically so a rep being honestly transparent about a constraint outside their control isn't scored identically to a rep being dismissively vague -- those are not the same behavior and were previously conflated under one 'partial' verdict.

evaluation_order.logic: Check specific-ownership terms first. If matched -> pass, done, no LLM call. If no specific match, check vague-ownership terms -- if matched, proceed to step 2. If neither list matches at all -> fail, done, no LLM call.

coaching_output.fail_no_match: Deterministic template: 'No ownership of next steps was stated before the call ended -- always name who owns the follow-up.'

evaluation_order.condition: Only runs if step 1 matched a vague-ownership term. Most calls skip this step entirely.
evaluation_order.question: The agent used vague language about next steps ('{matched_term}'). Considering the full context of this line and surrounding turns: is the agent being transparently honest about a genuine constraint outside their control while still taking personal accountability, or being dismissively vague to avoid commitment?

coaching_output.transparent_honest: Being upfront that this depends on another team, while still personally committing to follow up, is exactly the right way to handle something outside your control -- keep doing this.
coaching_output.dismissive: Vague ownership phrase used ('{matched_term}') without real accountability -- next time, even without a timeline, commit personally: 'I don't have an exact timeline, but I'll personally make sure you hear back.'

templates.partial: One interruption detected at {timestamp} while the customer was describing their issue -- let them finish before responding.
templates.fail: {count} interruptions detected during the customer's opening turns (first at {timestamp}) -- give the customer the full problem statement before jumping in.

coaching_output.note: Routes to manager review instead of a coaching_note.

evaluation_order.condition: Only runs if step 1 found no match.

coaching_output.prompt_addition: Return a `coaching_note`. On 'pass', reinforce the specific line that showed good warmth/professionalism. On 'partial'/'fail', cite the specific moment tone dipped and suggest a concrete alternative phrasing.

demo_notes.breakdown: Resolution Effectiveness always runs (1). Ownership only calls LLM if a vague-ownership term matched (0 or 1). Tone step 2 only runs if the hostile check was clean (0 or 1).
demo_notes.best_case: 1 call -- hostile hit on Tone (skips step 2) AND Ownership hit a specific term or no term at all (skips step 2).
demo_notes.worst_case: 3 calls -- clean tone, vague ownership match needing the honest/dismissive judgment call, plus resolution.
